open_questions: Soft Winds' head (Bishop's 'kicks and set ups') and Let's Cool One's solo were read but not written as songs: their bars mix sixteenths and triplets.
Gone's 'Philly Joe beat, with the rim click on 4' under the trumpet solo is named but not transcribed by Bishop; the song's version is the cymbal and foot of his bridge with the rim click added.
His triplet runs at 220 and up (Gaza Strip, Locomotion, Minority) are past the catalogue's ten notes a second and are approximated as rolls or eighths.
Equipment beyond Bishop's description (a 22-inch bass drum, 13- and 16-inch toms, a 20-inch ride) is not sourced: the brand of his 1950s kit is left out.
Bishop's other Philly Joe transcriptions (Hi-Groove Low Feedback, Dance of the Infidels, Stablemates, Sub City, Blue Roz, East of Brooklyn) were found and not used.

identity.name: Philly Joe Jones
identity.summary: The drummer of Miles Davis's first great quintet (1955-58) with Coltrane, Garland and Chambers, and on Blue Note and Riverside records with Coltrane, Rollins, Lee Morgan, Chet Baker and Bill Evans: a solid quarter-note pulse on the ride, the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4, the bass drum feathered, comps on the "and"s, stick shots and rudiments in the breaks, a polished brush technique. Davis's and Evans's favourite drummer. A leader from 1958, in London and Paris 1967-72, and the founder of Dameronia in 1981; he died in 1985.

alter_egos.name: Philly Joe
alter_egos.context: For his home town, to tell him from the older drummer Papa Jo Jones.

traditions.impact: A featured tap dancer on a Philadelphia radio show as a child.
Three or four years on the road with Joe Morris's band, then Tiny Grimes, Bull Moose Jackson and Arnett Cobb: Bishop hears 'a very substantive, deep R&B sound'.
'snare drum oriented, and rudiment oriented'; much of his vocabulary is in Charley Wilcoxon's books (Bishop).

eras.label: Cafe Society and the R&B road
eras.context: House drummer at Cafe Society with Tadd Dameron and the bebop players; rhythm-and-blues bands on the road.

eras.label: The Miles Davis Quintet and Blue Note
eras.context: Miles Davis's first great quintet with Coltrane, Garland and Chambers; sideman on Blue Note and Riverside records with Coltrane, Rollins, Lee Morgan, Hank Mobley, Chet Baker and Bill Evans.
defining_traits: the ride with a solid quarter-note pulse

eras.label: Leader, Europe and Dameronia
eras.context: His own groups from 1958; Bill Evans; London and Paris 1967-72; Evans again 1976 and 1978; Dameronia from 1981.

evidence.note: 'everything is lined up, and he's not fluffing the more technical stuff'.

swing.notes: 'His cymbal beat is fairly straight, with a solid quarter note pulse— with an emphasis on the skip note when playing in 2'; at 264 on Oleo the lead-in 'completely straight', the time swung 'slightly'.

dynamics.balance: Assertive in a supporting role; the accents lighter after the top of a chorus (Bishop on Oleo).

feel_profile.interaction: Comping as 'an expression of the changes, the form, of forward momentum' rather than conversation: the bass drum on 4 and the snare on the 'and' of 1, the 'and's of 2 and 4 at the ends of phrases, the one strong at the top of a solo (Bishop on Gaza Strip).

hand_techniques.name: Stick shots
hand_techniques.description: One stick laid on the head and struck with the other: on 1 of a break, in runs (Minority, Gaza Strip, Locomotion).

hand_techniques.name: Rudiments on the snare
hand_techniques.description: Six-stroke rolls with strong accents and slurred rolls, flat flams, ruffs, press rolls (Gaza Strip, Gone, Let's Cool One).

hand_techniques.name: Brushes
hand_techniques.description: A polished brush technique: a tremolo with one hand and accents with the other; the brush laid on the head and rolled with the palm (Soft Winds).

coordination.notes: The ride and the foot on 2 and 4 as an ostinato under snare and bass drum comps; the feet keep going under the breaks, and much of the break vocabulary is linear between the snare and bass drum (Bishop on Minority).

searched: Todd Bishop's transcriptions, read bar by bar: Gaza Strip (intro, top of the solos, Morgan's five choruses), Minority (two eight-bar breaks), Gone (head, bars 1-12; the rest looked over), Locomotion (intro), Soft Winds (brush solo), The Theme and Oleo (chorus entrances), Asiatic Raes (the Afro 6/8, two bars)
Looked over, not read bar by bar: Minority's fours, Soft Winds' head (kicks and set-ups), Let's Cool One's solo (page 1)
devices_search.note: No device written: no cross-rhythm, grouping or metric device across a bar line in the bars read. Gaza Strip's top-of-solo accents a dotted quarter apart last under two beats; Bishop's Sub City post describes a 'syncopated meter-within-meter lick' and a 'quarter note triplet lick', but that PDF was not read, so neither is recorded.

foot_techniques.name: Feathered bass drum, hi-hat on 2 and 4
foot_techniques.description: 'Jones mostly plays the hihat on 2 and 4 and feathers quarter notes on the bass drum throughout' (Let's Cool One); the feet keep going under the breaks (Minority).

aesthetic: a 50s A. Zildjian ride, bright and complex
sound_profile.cymbal_character: 'often a 20″ ride, with a moderately bright, complex 50s A. sound' (Bishop).

sample_hints.50s: A jazz kit with a 22-inch bass drum, a crusty snare, a bright 20-inch ride.

signature_traits.label: The rim click on 4
signature_traits.description: 'that Philly Joe beat, with the rim click on 4' under the cymbal (Gone).

signature_traits.label: The bass drum on 4, the snare on the "and" of 1
signature_traits.description: A punctuation he repeats across choruses (Gaza Strip).

signature_traits.label: The top of a chorus
signature_traits.description: A fill or roll on the last bar, the one strong, then big accents on 4 and in the next bar (Oleo, The Theme, Gaza Strip).

signature_traits.label: Stick shots
signature_traits.description: Stick shots on 1 of a break and in runs (Minority, Gaza Strip, Locomotion).

patterns.name: Gaza Strip: comping under Morgan
patterns.function: The ride and the foot on 2 and 4, the snare on the "and" of 1 and the bass drum on 4.

evidence.note: Bishop solo bars 6, 18, 31; his 'bass drum on 4, followed by a snare drum accent on the & of 1' in one bar.

patterns.name: Gaza Strip: the intro, stick shots
patterns.function: Stick shots, then the snare, the bass drum between.

evidence.note: Bishop bar 5; one bass drum note and one snare stroke left out for air.

patterns.name: Asiatic Raes: Philly Joe's Afro 6
patterns.function: The bell, a rim click on 2, the bass drum on 1 and 4, the floor tom on 5 and 6.

evidence.note: Bishop's first bar; the second adds the bell on 4.

patterns.name: Gone: that Philly Joe beat
patterns.function: The ride, the foot on 2 and 4 and the rim click on 4.

evidence.note: Bishop names it and leaves it out ('give that a close listen'); his bridge (bars 36-49) has the cymbal and the foot.

patterns.name: Oleo: the lead-in, straight eighths
patterns.function: Accented straight eighths on the snare from 2, into the top of the chorus.

evidence.note: Bishop's image; at 264 the eighths 'completely straight'.

patterns.name: Locomotion: the intro, bar 1
patterns.function: RRLL RRLL on the snare and the high tom, accents on 1 and 3.

patterns.name: Minority: a break, stick shots and the snare
patterns.function: A stick shot on 1, then the snare on the "and"s, the hi-hat on 2 and 4.

evidence.note: Bishop bar 1; his feathered bass drum on every beat left out.

patterns.name: Soft Winds: the palm roll
patterns.function: Triplets on the low tom, the brush laid on the head and rolled with the palm.

equipment.label: His 1950s kit (Bishop)
equipment.layout_notes: Bishop: 'He generally uses larger drums— a 22″ bass drum, and 13 and 16″ tom toms. Not necessarily real big cymbals— often a 20″ ride, with a moderately bright, complex 50s A. sound.' No brand sourced for the drums.

affiliations.name: The Miles Davis Quintet
affiliations.notes: Davis's favourite drummer, in his autobiography.

affiliations.name: Bill Evans
affiliations.notes: Everybody Digs Bill Evans (1958); tours in 1976 and 1978. Evans too called him his favourite drummer.

affiliations.name: Dameronia
affiliations.notes: A band for Tadd Dameron's music, which he founded and led.

evidence.note: 'He seems to have wrapped up and finished a lot things created by Max Roach, Kenny Clarke, and Art Blakey.'
Bishop sees 'vestiges of the showy, classy, vaudeville thing I associate with Papa Jo Jones' in his brushes.
Goodman: Williams modelled Philly Joe's creativity.

philosophy.idea: Comping is an expression of the changes, the form and forward momentum, closer to groove than to conversation with the soloist.
Set the band up to come back in: a break's last bar or two says it is ending.

innovations: The hard core of 1950s bop drumming: the Miles Davis Quintet's time, comping and chorus entrances, 'so much of his playing = normal jazz vocabulary now'
Rudimental snare vocabulary in small-group jazz

cultural_references.description: Miles Davis and Bill Evans each called him his favourite drummer.

common_misconceptions: That his style is plain: 'The stuff is so familiar that he becomes invisible' (Bishop).

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A 1950s jazz kit, a 22-inch bass drum, a crusty snare, a bright 20-inch ride
generation_rules: The foot on 2 and 4 and a solid quarter-note pulse on the ride.
Comps on the "and"s; the bass drum on 4 and the snare on the "and" of 1.
A fill or roll into the top of a chorus, the one strong, accents after.
Stick shots and rudiments in the breaks.
avoid: A rock backbeat on the snare

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Max Roach's, Kenny Clarke's and Art Blakey's bebop, finished; after him Tony Williams, Jack DeJohnette, and every drummer who learned the Miles Davis Quintet records.
